note.headline: We hear email is only being read by AI agents.
body: So I wrote you a card instead.

I'm Brian, and I work with brand and creative teams at Frontify. After reading what Atlassian has shared this year, a few ideas stuck with me. They're guesses, not conclusions. You know your world better than I do.
If one of them is interesting, I'd love to compare notes.
note.emailLine: You're seeing this from my email. It's the same page I left on a card at your San Francisco office.

ideas.title: Brand context inside the AI tools your team already uses
ideas.summary: People ask Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot. Frontify quietly supplies the brand rules, messaging and approved assets.

why.text: Atlassian's Team '26 Europe update framed AI as multiplayer work, where agents join teams with clear identity and scoped access.

looksLike: Guidelines, approved assets and messaging live in one place, structured for people and readable by AI.
Frontify's MCP server lets tools like Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor look up brand rules and approved assets. It's read-only by default, and an admin decides when to turn it on.
An agent drafting a page pulls from the same source your brand team already maintains.
ideas.question: When an agent drafts marketing content today, where does it get your brand rules?

demo.q: What tone should a launch post use?
demo.a: Bold, optimistic and practical, with a wink. Use plain language and skip the jargon.
demo.note: Answer drawn from Atlassian's public voice and tone guidance, for illustration.

ideas.title: Approved messaging at the start of the brief
ideas.summary: Your tools run the work. Frontify can hold the brand context the work starts from.

why.text: Atlassian's own marketing post says more AI tools alone won't fix coordination, and that work should start from the right brief and approved messaging.

looksLike: Messaging, guidelines and approved assets sit in a living brand portal that teams link to from their briefs.
Creative reviews run as approval requests with clear reviewers and deadlines.
Frontify connects to Jira Cloud, so brand work and the tickets around it stay linked.
ideas.question: Where does approved messaging live today, and who keeps it current?

ideas.title: One current home for a family of app brands
ideas.summary: Jira, Confluence, Loom, Rovo and more, each with its own logo and rules.

why.text: Atlassian's public design system documents a shared logo system across its apps, plus separate rules for Marketplace partners.

looksLike: A brand hub with a page per app, all inheriting the parent brand.
Internal-only logo sets stay internal through permissions, while partners get a view made for them.
Update a logo once and every portal shows the current version.
ideas.question: When a team or partner needs the current Loom or Rovo logo, where do they go?

ideas.title: Event content without the request queue
ideas.summary: Two Team '26 events this year means a lot of speaker cards, slides and signage.

why.text: Atlassian ran Team '26 in the US in May and Team '26 Europe in Amsterdam on Oct 6 to 8.

looksLike: Designers build templates once, with brand elements locked.
Event and field teams fill them in from a browser, including motion versions for social.
Your creative team spends its time on the work only it can do.
ideas.question: How many event assets does your team still build by hand for a Team event?

hero.sub: Most people at Atlassian will never open Frontify. They'll ask Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot, and Frontify makes sure the answer already knows your brand.
hero.prompt: Draft a LinkedIn post for our next Rovo feature launch.
hero.generic: Excited to announce an amazing new feature! Our innovative AI solution will revolutionize the way your team works. Don't miss out! #Innovation #AI #Teamwork
hero.onbrand: Rovo just learned a new trick. Ask it a question and it pulls the answer from work your team already did. No digging, no tab maze. Try it this week and tell us what it should learn next.

check.note: Brand Check is in beta. The asset, findings and guidelines here are samples built from Atlassian's public design system, not Atlassian's own.

contexts.title: Every kind of context, in one place
contexts.sub: Brand, creative, product and event guidance live in {name}'s portal, plus an Everyday section with short versions for every employee. People read them, and AI tools answer from them.
contexts.note: Sample pages built from Atlassian's public design system and product names. Not Atlassian's own guidelines.

items.label: Brand
items.title: Our palette
items.lead: Brand blue leads. Neutrals carry most of the page.
items.rule: Use Brand blue for primary actions and links only.
items.ask: What blue do I use for a button?
items.answer: Use **Brand blue, #1868DB**, for primary buttons and links.

items.label: Creative
items.title: Photography
items.lead: Real teams doing real work, never staged.

do.label: Teams at work
do.note: Candid moments of people working together.

dont.label: Posed for the camera
dont.note: No staged handshakes or stock smiles.

items.ask: Can I use a stock photo of a handshake?
items.answer: Better not. The photography guidelines ask for **candid teamwork**, and **no staged handshakes or stock smiles**.

items.label: Product
items.title: Rovo positioning
items.lead: Start every launch brief from this page.
items.positioning: Rovo is AI that works across the apps teams already use, with the context of their work.
claims: Works across Jira, Confluence and Loom
Answers from your team's own content
items.rule: Always write Rovo, never "the Rovo AI."
items.ask: Write a one-line pitch for Rovo.
items.answer: **Rovo is AI that works across the apps your team already uses, with the context of your work.** Drafted from the approved positioning.

items.label: Everyday
items.title: Email tone of voice
items.lead: The short version of our tone of voice, for everyone who sends email.
rules: Say what you need in under eight words.
Lead with the ask or the answer.
Use the standard signature. No quotes or images.
items.do: Can you review the launch plan by Thursday?
items.dont: Just circling back on the below!!
items.askLabel: Before sending, in Outlook with Copilot
items.ask: Check this email against our writing guidelines.
items.answer: Two fixes before you send: **put the ask in the first line**, and **use the standard signature**.
